answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. A signal from completed work then raises limits gradually, while fraud or coordinated abuse burns the stake and resets that identity’s standing. Splitting into many accounts no longer creates free influence: the attacker must immobilize capital in every account and risks losing it. Like a jetty resisting a hollow tide, the barrier is costly to cross, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
